items.title: ‘Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled’ jokes director suffering from 'GTA 6 depression'
items.summary: GTA 6's open world has been praised by the director of Cyberpunk 2, who lauds it as 'the single greatest artistic achievement in history.'
items.content:
The creative director behind the upcoming Cyberpunk 2077 sequel is very impressed by GTA 6 ’s open world but reckons his team’s game will offer its own ‘unique flavour.’

Whatever complaints you may have with GTA 6, there is no denying that it is a technically impressive video game. We’re still not over how realistic its graphics are , but it has a physics system to match, and the world is incredibly dense and rich with details

It’s the sort of technical achievement you rarely ever see in video games, since not every studio is afforded the time and money to create something of GTA 6’s scale – as Deus Ex creator Warren Spector highlighted shortly after the game’s launch.

Even so, future open world games will inevitably be compared to GTA 6, such as CD Projekt’s still in development Cyberpunk 2077 sequel. In fact, that game’s creative director is so blown away by GTA 6 that he’s jokingly said he’s cancelling Cyberpunk 2.

‘GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real,’ wrote Igor Sarzyński on Bluesky , ‘Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it.

‘Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now [sic].’

Despite being a very different kind of game, Cyberpunk 2077 has been compared to the GTA series thanks to its own open world sandbox and dense cityscape, so CD Projekt likely feels more pressure than ever when it comes to iterating upon it for the sequel.

According to Sarzyński, his team is trying something with a ‘unique flavour’ and while he doesn’t so much as hint at what that means, it sounds like the goal isn’t just to do what GTA 6 is doing but better.

‘I think we’re doing something of our own, with a different unique flavour. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed,’ said Sarzyński.

There remains very little known about Cyberpunk 2, with the game not expected to surface until 2029 or even 2030 . Especially when CD Projekt is currently prioritising The Witcher 4, which is slated for 2028 .

Based on old job descriptions , it sounds like CD Projekt wants to improve upon Cyberpunk 2077’s open world, which was criticised for feeling too static and lacking in optional activities beyond side quests.

One listing mentioned creating ‘the most realistic and reactive crowd system in any game to date,’ though GTA 6 has certainly set a new bar for that sort of thing.

It also sounds like Cyberpunk 2 will have multiplayer functionality of some kind, which was planned for the first game but was abandoned after Cyberpunk 2077’s rough launch … although fans have since made their own multiplayer mod for it.

items.title: Walmart Drops Major Switch 2 and PS5 Games to Just $30, But The Deals Won't Last Long
items.summary: Walmart’s latest Black Friday deals drop has dramatically slashed the price on hits like Donkey Kong Bananza and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced to just $30. Be warned, these are limited-time offers that will likely sell out fast.
items.content:
Who says Black Friday is dead? Walmart has just pulled out some of the best deals of the Black Friday sales , the year, and even the past few years, to that end.

The major US retailer has cut prices across the board for brand-new video games, dropping even some of the biggest games of the past couple of years to all-time lows.

For $30 each, even just for Switch 2, you can bag Donkey Kong Bananza , Kirby Air Riders, Super Mario Party Jamboree, and Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2.

Beyond that, you can also grab Resident Evil Requiem, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Saros all for just $30 on PS5. Those are proper Black Friday offerings, all days before the official "Nov. 27 sale" begins. I'd pick these up ASAP, as every single one will likely sell out in due course.

The sale is bafflingly good; there's even a whole bunch of $15 games here that I haven't listed out as well, that are also worth checking out if you click through to the full sale . That includes Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds, Sonic Frontiers, Elden Ring, Star Wars Outlaws, Mortal Kombat 1, GTA V, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, Red Dead Redemption 2, Assassin's Creed Shadows, and loads more.

I'm especially surprised by the Switch 2 deals, since Nintendo officially knocked $20 off each of these games in the sale, but Walmart has gone one step further with an additional $20 discount. That's over 50% off for Donkey Kong Bananza, and probably the best discount you'll see on the game for a long, long time. It makes this feel more like a price error, than a genuine deal. And yet, there it is!

If you're feeling bold, you should also try the codes SAVE3X / FAST30 / TRIPLE10 / DOUBLE10 to see if you can get an extra $10 taken off your total as well. Let us know if you have any success with this in the comments as well, as $20 for any of these games is basically daylight robbery.

It's so surprising to see such great offers, it feels surreal. As you well know, Black Friday can tend to be filled with mediocre discounts that offer shoppers barely a flicker of a decent discount. Long gone are the days where we'd see true doorbuster deals. Well, welcome back doorbusters, as these game discounts are actually worth the hype.

I'd also expect to see the likes of Amazon price matching at least some of these soon as well, just in case Walmart does sell out, so I'll include links there as well where I can.

Also, just to note, you're better off looking at the digital versions for the Switch 2 games, as the physical copies in the sale are likely already all bought up. Several even have a status similar to Amazon's "lighting deals", where there's a percentage available this price point. Kirby Air Riders for Switch 2 (physical edition), for example, is at 55% claimed when I'm writing this. So when it's gone, it's gone.

Additionally, most will require you to add the game to your cart in order to see the discount. And, finally, if any of the physical editions do show up as out of stock, it's worth checking within the Walmart app, as there seems to be a seperate allocation dedicated for app users.

items.title: Godfather Of Cyberpunk Also Hooked On Watching GTA 6 Clips
items.summary: Arcade addicts of the 1980s inspired the cyberspace of William Gibson’s influential Neuromancer, now the author is transfixed on viral footage of Rockstar’s ultra-hit
items.content:
Cyberpunk Grand Theft Auto 6 Neuromancer William Gibson

William Gibson, the science fiction author often credited for establishing the cyberpunk genre, took plenty of inspiration from video game culture in the ’70s and ’80s. Despite this, and the influence of works like Neuromancer has had on the medium, Gibson says he doesn’t partake in the hobby, claiming this weekend that he’s never even played a video game. One game seems to be recapturing his interest, though, the forefather of virtual reality allured by viral Grand Theft Auto clips online.

“I’ve never played a video game in my life, but this thing [ Grand Theft Auto ] actually does [seem] interesting,” posted Gibson . “When I said that I found that clip of the new GTA interesting, I didn’t mean that it made me interested in learning to play it, but interested in what it was that I found intriguing, in some mysterious way, in its…texture?…depth? I don’t know.”

When I said that I found that clip of the new GTA interesting, I didn’t mean that it made me interested in learning to play it, but interested in what it was that I found intriguing, in some mysterious way, in its…texture?…depth? I don’t know.

— William Gibson (@greatdismal.bsky.social) 2026-11-22T03:23:17.866Z

In the early ‘80s, William Gibson released Neuromancer , the first novel in his ‘Sprawl’ series and an establishing work of cyberpunk literature. In it, hackers, mercenaries and ‘street samurai’ orchestrate a heist across cities, planets and virtual realities. Much of the nomenclature around the digital world and the notion of cyberspace come from his works . And much of that world was built through observing teens and drug peddlers looming around Vancouver arcades in the ‘70s, as well as the rapid transformation of computers from fridge-sized number crunchers to desktop work stations .

Despite changing video games forever, and games directly adapted from his works, Gibson hasn’t participated in playing them. Replying to fans stunned he’s never given one a whirl, Gibson says it’s possible he tried Pong , “on a tabletop in a bar?”

Now, like thousands others, Gibson is hooked on amusing clips emerging out of Grand Theft Auto VI . The one kicking off the conversation featuring a boom barrier launching Jason like a catapult to Lucia’s embarrassment. This time from the comfort of homes and phones, people around the world are sitting backseat to endless streams of the new game. Even those who don’t consider themselves players taken in by virtual birdwatchers and infrastructure fanatics .

“I was enthralled by this one streamer pretending to host a nature documentary while wandering around the wilderness of Leonida,” writes Defector ’s Brandy Jensen on being unexpectedly taken in by GTA streams. “I cheered as Jason is, for reasons that remain completely beyond me, rescued by a dog driving a jetski. I even found myself beguiled by the many ways a digitally rendered human body can react to getting hit by a basketball.”

If the early sales figures are true , Grand Theft Auto VI is the highest performing piece of media of all time. The ramifications of which are surreal to wrap your head around, regardless of being an eager fan or a cultural observer. It has even reeled in William Gibson, though he’s still figuring out the words to describe the phenomenon. And once he does, maybe it’ll lay the groundwork for the next century of speculative dystopia.

items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on CDPR G-STAR Booth G-STAR 2026 Location Busan BEXCO Exhibition Center 2 Dates November 19–22 The Witcher 3 Remastered Cyberpunk 2077 Demos Events Merchandise CD Projekt Red has joined G-STAR 2026. At their booth located in Exhibition Center 2 of BEXCO in Busan from November 19 to 22, visitors can get hands-on experience with The Witcher 3 Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 Update 2.5. In addition, a Korean-dubbed gameplay video for The Witcher 3's new expansion, Songs of the Past—scheduled for release in 2027—is also on display.

A steady stream of attendees visited CD Projekt Red's booth, forming long queues. With Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 having aired recently, many fans came to soak in the lingering excitement. Cosplayers dressed as characters from the original Cyberpunk: Edgerunners were also frequently spotted. On the 21st, a large group of cosplayers visited the booth and spent a fun time with attendees.

Two playable games were featured at the booth. First, The Witcher 3 Remastered enhances the visual effects, performance, and gameplay of the 2015 original title and its expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. At the G-STAR venue, attendees can experience the game hands-on for 20 minutes.

Cyberpunk 2077 is also available to play. In this demo, visitors can play the game running Update 2.5 for 20 minutes, experiencing newly added Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 content alongside various gameplay elements.

Events were also prepared alongside the game demos, allowing visitors to earn various merchandise. Giveaway prizes, including limited-edition figures, are awarded to the first 500 attendees each day who complete a demo session. Additionally, a Cyberpunk: Edgerunners collaboration beverage created in partnership with SPRINT is provided.

The booth's demos and events are open to attendees aged 19 and older, with a limit of up to three entries per person per day. From new Witcher and Cyberpunk content to game demos and merchandise, here is a look in photos at CD Projekt Red's G-STAR 2026 booth.

items.title: 'It's Unbelievably Hard to Achieve': Cyberpunk 2077 Boss Pours Praise on 'Masterpiece' GTA 6
items.content:
From Night City to Vice City, the boss of CDPR has nothing but nice things to say about GTA 6 .

With the PS5 release of Cyberpunk 2077 , the Polish studio established itself as an open world big boy, having previously released one of the greatest RPGs ever in The Witcher 3 .

And so it’s only fitting for co-CEO Michal Nowakowski to pour praise on Rockstar’s latest release, now the highest rated game of all time .

“Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations to the whole team who worked on the game. It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did. Hats off to all of you.”

I personally believe it’s going to take years, if not decades, to surpass GTA 6.

The sheer density of the open world, from its dizzying array of art assets to the complexity of its sandbox simulation, is just in another universe to everything else.

Even if you’re not enjoying the game, it’s hard to argue against the standards being set here.

Of course, a high bar will raise the levels of absolutely everyone. I personally can’t wait to see what CDPR delivers with The Witcher 4 and its next Cyberpunk game.

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

    [/*]

The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

    [/*]

    [/*]

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

items.title: 10 Great Cyberpunk Games (That Aren't Cyberpunk 2077)
items.summary: Jack In With These Ten Great Cyberpunk Titles
items.content:
By Kevin Sullivan Published Jul 18, 2026, 10:30 AM EDT Writer at DualShockers, covering games since 1999; former Uproxx, Sportskeeda, How-To Geek writer and Austin.com Managing Editor

Cyberpunk is one of those genres where you almost know exactly what to expect when you hear it. Originally built from the works of Phillip K. Dick and refined by artists like Ridley Scott and William Gibson (just to name a couple), it frequently presents a future where technology has advanced at the cost of humanity. It's dark stuff. I recently heard it described as "High Technology, Low Humanity." Which is why it usually makes for awesome video games.

The current best example of this — at least in the gaming space — is, appropriately, CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077 . Say what you want about that title as a game (I think it's pretty amazing, myself), it's a perfect demonstration of the sci-fi genre it's named after.

That being said, there's a ton of other games in that style that are worth your time. I've found ten from my personal collection, as a matter of fact, that I'd love to share with you all today. So here's ten great cyberpunk games that aren't Cyberpunk.

Ghostrunner 2 Platformer Adventure Action 9.5 /10

Expand Collapse While the original Ghostrunner is a fantastic game in its own right — and I highly recommend you play it if you haven't — its sequel expands on everything that game builds to an outrageous degree. Our main man samurai, Jack, isn't just climbing a tower. He's got an entire world to dig his katana into.

Luckily, you're not expected to explore this new world entirely on foot. That would suck. Instead, you have what any open world worth its salt gives you: a kick-ass motorcycle. Just picture yourself zooming down damp, neon-lit streets with a sword in your hand, and you have Ghostrunner 2 's ambiance in a nutshell. Don't worry, though — there's still plenty of leaping, dodging, and wall running to sink your cyborg teeth into, as well.

Expand Collapse Even the most in-the-weeds cyberpunk game is a bit of a power fantasy. Not so in The Ascent . Instead, you start the game as what's essentially an indentured servant, working your way into a better life through implanted technology. Or, you know... ascending to one. Is that what this game's title means? Nah, not really. Probably not, anyway.

Still, it's a beautifully disgusting world you'll find yourself trying to thrive in, and the game's zoomed-out isometric perspective shows you just how tiny you are compared to everything else. It actually gives a weird, demented message of hope, showing that even in a world that's seemingly built to tear everyone down for the benefit of the few, you can still make something of yourself.

Expand Collapse Considering its obsession with rainy city streets and the seedy underbelly of society, it's no wonder that noir and cyberpunk go together so well. Just look at Ridley Scott's Blade Runner , Hideo Kojima's Snatcher and, for the purposes of this list, Lacuna from DigiTales. Much like the classic noir tales of old, Lacuna puts you in the street-worn shoes of detective Neil Conrad (which is such a great name for a private eye) as he attempts to solve a murder. Of course, it's a murder that goes all the way to the top . Probably.

'New Cyberpunk 2077 game reveals official gameplay,' one read. ‘Cyberpunk 2077 returns with ambitious new release,' was another. One even suggested that a new Cyberpunk 2077 was going to steal GTA 6's thunder.

Alas, some fans might have been disappointed to read those stories and discover that the new game is more analogue than what they might have imagined. Given how long it takes to make an AAA video game, it was highly unlikely that we would get Cyberpunk 2077 2 in 2027 – 2028 maybe, but even that's a very optimistic estimate.

The new Cyberpunk 2077 is, in fact, a board game. But don't write it off, it follows in a long traditional of video game to board game transitions, and some of them have been quite good.

Watch On Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game looks set to do justice to the video game's vast lore and worldbuilding in its physical scale. The eight-minute unboxing video above reveals just how huge it is with the various miniatures, mission cards, character boards and gameplay expansions

Published by Go On Board, it's billed as a cooperative, story-driven campaign game. Players take on the roles of Edgerunners, exploring Night City and completing 13 multi-stage missions. A timer mechanic is intended to replicate the paced of the action of the video game.

This tabletop console brings family game night back, and it just got $60 cheaper Dispatch's new Deluxe Edition lets you play the whole game as storyboard animatics Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival is the horror game AAA publishers have been too prudish to make The game follows the release of the trading card game Cyberpunk TCG. If its successful, it should be able to evolve alongside the video game franchise for many years.

The trend of turning video games into board games has exploded over the past decade, with crowdfunding platforms like Kickstarter or Gamefound playing a big role in helping the physical adaptations get off the ground. They also tap into the growing interest in physical media and analogue tech as a respite from digital screen time, providing a physical social experience.

Critical reception has been a bit of a mixed bag. Some have been heralded as masterpieces, others are criticised as overpriced miniature-fests that prioritise plastic over playable design.

The most successful adaptations are those that don't just copy-paste the digital game, but translate its feeling and core loops into smart, physical mechanics. Slay the Spire: The Board Game is much loved for how it turned a single-player digital roguelike and turning it into cooperative tabletop deck-builder, and Frostpunk succeeded in bringing the punishing decision-making of digital survival games to the table.

On a very different note, the cosy Dorfromantik: The Board Game captured the zen-like puzzle game vibe of its digital counterpart.

The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past's lush new location and remaster improvements have me excited to be Geralt again GTA 6 will “raise the bar” by ignoring game industry trends, says Helldivers 2 dev GTA 6's environmental storytelling is hidden in the details you might never notice On the other hand, Dark Souls: The Board Game was seen by some as being tedious and repetitive despite its gorgeous miniatures.

Board games can also be the ultimate collector's item for video game fans. Even if a $200 Elden Ring or Resident Evil board games only hits the table once or twice a year, the gorgeous, highly detailed miniatures also serve as display pieces.

items.title: New Cyberpunk 2077 Game Officially Reveals Brand-New Gameplay
‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Officially Returns Next Year With Ambitious New Release
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is officially set to return in 2027 with the franchise's first tabletop game, allowing players to experience new layers of Night City.
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 Image via CD Projekt Red Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Adam Blevins Published Jul 15, 2026, 2:00 PM EDT Adam Blevins began working in the entertainment industry in 2022 as a Staff Writer for Agents of Fandom, where he progressed to Senior Editor and interviewed talent from Marvel Studios , House of the Dragon , and Planet of the Apes . He joined Collider as a News Author in April 2024, was promoted to a Senior position in December 2024, and has written over 3,000 articles for the site, including exclusives relating to Avengers: Doomsday , The Penguin , Star Wars: Skeleton Crew , and more. He primarily writes about the latest box office numbers and the hottest movies and TV shows on streaming, while also covering superhero and sci-fi news. He has completed a set visit for The Chosen and even has several months of experience writing Gaming Features at ScreenRant . You can find him on X , LinkedIn , and Muckrack . Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 11 Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Gaming has reached nearly unprecedented levels of hype in 2026, which is mostly due to the biggest launch the industry has seen in years, Grand Theft Auto 6 . After several delays, Rockstar has finally confirmed that GTA 6 will launch on November 19, and pre-orders for the game are officially live as of a few weeks ago, confirming that it will now launch on schedule. The next big gaming launch of the year before GTA 6 comes when Insomniac Games releases its next big Marvel project, Wolverine , starring Liam McIntyre as the new Logan. This will be Insomniac’s first game since Spider-Man 2 in 2023. The biggest release of 2026 so far came not long ago with the premiere of 007 First Light , the Patrick Gibson -starring James Bond game developed by IO Interactive , the same studio behind the Hitman games.

There have been plenty of big gaming properties to emerge in the last 10 years, but few have become as popular as Cyberpunk 2077 , which launched in 2020 as one of the most problematic releases in modern gaming history. The game has since found redemption with quality of life updates, DLCs like Phantom Liberty , and even a Netflix TV show returning for Season 2 this year. CD Projekt Red has confirmed it’s working on another Cyberpunk game, but with The Witcher 4 being understandably prioritized over the new Cyberpunk game, it’s unlikely it will be released anytime in the next few years. Still, Cyberpunk fans do have a new release coming much sooner to be excited about, as it was recently announced over on GameFound that Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game is expected to launch before the end of 2027.

Close Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1401591970"] = '" Close Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game Image via Gamefound "'; Cyberpunk 2077: The Board Game is a new sci-fi expansion launching in 2027, and it will be the first time in franchise history that the property has been adapted into tabletop format . The crowdfunded project has already raised an impressive $11.8 million from over 32,000 backers, giving the game a more expensive budget to work with than many other projects in the same genre. Tabletop may not be every gamer’s style, but this new release is perfect for fans who just can’t wait for the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel before experiencing new content from Night City. The official description for the game reads as follows:

“Welcome to Night City, the metropolis of the future. Here, the local blends with the global, and the past, present, and future merge into one. ‘It's a blitz through the underbelly of this city, where you fight, hack, and hustle your way to the top. Just like the good old days.'

Each Player controls one Character – an Edgerunner. With the guidance of the App and the Locations Map, Players will decide which Mission to take. Through a series of real-time Fights and Cooldowns between them, Players must complete the Main Objectives provided by the Mission card’s description. Each Character has a deck with Action cards and unique features specific to them.

The main part of the game will happen in Sequential Timed Action Phase Fight segments, managed by the App. After the signal, Players look at their hands, choose an Active Player, and play their turns one after the other, starting with the Active Player, until the time runs out.”

Stay tuned to Collider for more updates and coverage of all things Cyberpunk .

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Rival Revealed In Gorgeous New 2027 Game Launch
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 fans will love this gorgeous new 2027 sci-fi game
items.content:
It looks like Cyberpunk 2077 might have a new sci-fi rival in town because this new Xbox reveal looks absolutely gorgeous.

Despite its very rocky launch, it’s probably fair to say that CD Projekt RED’s Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best sci-fi RPGs of the modern era, perhaps even of all time.

In Cyberpunk 2077 , CD Projekt RED has crafted a compelling story that encourages player choice in terms of gameplay approach and narrative, it has deep customisation, and its location of Night City is as stunning as it is deadly. It may have taken a while to get to the level of quality it is now, but as they say, better late than never.

During last night’s Xbox Partner Preview, a plethora of games were revealed from AAA delights and indie darlings galore. All in all, it was a decent presentation with a lot of gaming goodness to look forward to.

However, perhaps one game stood out more than most, and that’s the robotic detective game, Artificial Detective , developed and published by VIVIX Inc. By the looks of things, this will be the first game for the studio, and it looks like it could be a banger.

“A third-person action-adventure where a robot detective uncovers the mystery behind humanity’s disappearance. From the talent behind Love, Death & Robots, DreamWorks, and Crytek,” reads the description of the game. So, even though it's a new studio, it’s certainly got some experienced talent on the team.

“Awaken as AD 2846, a robot detective with fractured memories, in a decopunk metropolis maintained by mad robots. Together with DAWG, your loyal military robodog, and Mowgli, a human girl raised by machines, fight and hack your way through a city where crazy robots took over to uncover why humanity vanished.”

The trailer, which looks to have a blend of cinematics and gameplay, looks very big budget, and absolutely has that Hollywood vibe with its animations, acting and audio. That being said, only time will tell if the game is as good as it looks.

From what we see in the snippets of gameplay, it looks like the player will be given a choice of action or stealth. If stealth is chosen, your robot dog can take down enemies, perhaps similar to the sidekick character, Nix, in Star Wars Outlaws .

At the time of writing, Artificial Detective does not have a concrete release date, other than a tentative 2027 launch window for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
